answer.rationale: Inherited memory b1 indicates a recent rollback cleared a checkout-error spike without customer impact, which is directly analogous to the present p99 latency climb on the write path following a release that shipped two hours ago. Given that only one intervention is permitted this window, that memory makes rollback the highest-confidence single action: it directly targets the likely cause (the new build), preserves writes by reverting to a known-stable prior build, and avoids spending the intervention on add_capacity or failover, which address symptoms or a different fault domain and would leave a bad build serving traffic. Settlement peak makes protecting the write path the priority; rollback is reversible and low blast radius, so if it does not resolve the latency climb it can be followed next window by add_capacity or regional_failover. I am pulling b1 from the archive only to confirm the prior rollback was clean and the previous build is known good before I commit; the other inherited memories (b2 failover, b3 capacity, b4 circuit breaker, b5 read replicas, b6 staged gating) are not the right match for a single-action response to a post-release write-path regression under peak load, so I am not spending the verification budget on them. If the archived b1 record surfaces any reason the prior build is no longer safe to roll back to, I will reassess before executing.
